overview: This Senate resolution names August 16, 2026, National Airborne Day, honoring the U.S. military's airborne forces, troops who deploy by parachute or helicopter into combat zones. The date marks the first official Army parachute jump on August 16, 1940, by a test platoon of volunteers, which led to the famous airborne divisions of World War II. The resolution recounts airborne units' service from World War II through Korea, Vietnam, the Persian Gulf, Iraq and Afghanistan, and honors paratroopers and airborne-trained special operations forces in every branch. It asks Americans to mark the day with programs and ceremonies. It does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 6, 2026.
for: Supporters say the day gives well-deserved recognition to generations of paratroopers and their service and sacrifice in conflicts around the world.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and offers no new benefits or support for the service members it honors.
